move: cube bursts into eight cubelets, spin and twist, snap back seamlessly
how: Eight CSS 3D cubelets (six faces each, brightness-shaded) form a 2x2x2 cube inside a group that turns 360deg on Y over the full 5s and nods rotationX 14deg yoyo. A state object drives placement through gsap.set in onUpdate: at 6% spread goes 0 to 1 with back.out(1.8) so each cubelet flies out along its octant to 2.6x the half-size; at 22% spin rotates each cubelet 180deg on Y (sign by position, expo.inOut) and at 30% twist does the same on X; at 58% spread returns with back.in(1.4) as the cubelets snap together; at 74-78% spin and twist run to 360, which is the rest pose, so the last frame equals the first. A soft floor shadow scales 1.35 and thins during the spread.
adapt: Change the eight face colours, cube size (H) and the spread factor (1.6); the stage gradient and shadow are the only other visuals; keep the back.out/back.in spread pair and the expo.inOut half-turns so the loop stays seamless.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the world, group and eight cubelets with perspective on el; animate returns the timeline with the proxy-state tweens at 0.06D, 0.22D, 0.3D, 0.58D, 0.74D, 0.78D and the Y turn spanning D. The placement is gsap.set inside onUpdate, which already lives on the timeline, so it ports directly; scope getElementById to el.
caveats: 48 faces with filter: brightness, moderate cost
